page: Amazon Web Services inf1.2xlarge is an instance within the inf1 family, utilizing the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8275CL processor with an x86_64 architecture, running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The configuration provides 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. System memory consists of 16.0 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include local storage or discrete GPUs, and it is provisioned with a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the inf1.2xlarge demonstrates mid-tier performance across most standardized tests. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests yielded average scores of 1495.28 and 7874.32, respectively. Memory performance is characterized by an average read-only small block bandwidth of 439.45 GB/sec, which drops to 50.99 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, alongside a write bandwidth of 38.4 GB/sec. Geekbench testing aligns with these average metrics, showing a single-core score of 1211.0 and a multi-core score of 4565.0. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression registered as weak at 30.03 GB/sec, and LLM inference benchmarks using a medium 7B model showed poor to weak results, with prompt processing at 11.45 tokens/sec and text generation at 6.67 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the inf1.2xlarge offers a balanced compute-to-memory ratio of 1:2, making it a viable option for workloads that require dedicated CPU resources without massive memory footprints. Given the average performance in database operations and static web serving throughput, this instance is suited for general-purpose compute tasks, basic web serving, and lightweight text or image processing. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which should be factored into the overall architectural design.

Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it features 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, 16.0 GB of DDR4 RAM, and a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, with no local storage or discrete GPUs. Performance benchmarks generally fall into the average range, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 4565.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 8870.98. With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance provides a balanced hardware profile for general-purpose compute, static web serving, and light database operations where dedicated CPU allocation is required without high memory overhead.
